lines.text: Lesson six: entry, exit, and profit or loss. Let's do the maths, step by step.
lines.say: Lesson six: entry, exit, and profit or loss. Let's do the maths, step by step.

lines.text: Every trade has a start and an end. The question is always: how much did it make, or lose?
lines.say: Every trade has a start and an end. The question is always: how much did it make, or lose?

lines.text: To answer, you need four things: entry, exit, size and fees. Let's meet them one by one.
lines.say: To answer, you need four things: entry, exit, size and fees. Let's meet them one by one.

lines.text: The entry price is the price where you open a trade. The exit price is where you close it.
lines.say: The entry price is the price where you open a trade. The exit price is where you close it.

lines.text: Think of a bus ride: where you get on, and where you get off. The distance between them matters.
lines.say: Think of a bus ride: where you get on, and where you get off. The distance between them matters.

lines.text: Here, you enter at 60,000. The price moves, and you exit at 61,200. A move of 1,200 USDT.
lines.say: Here, you enter at sixty thousand. The price moves, and you exit at sixty-one thousand two hundred. A move of one thousand two hundred U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Size is how much you trade. Quantity is the amount of the asset, like 0.05 BTC.
lines.say: Size is how much you trade. Quantity is the amount of the asset, like zero point zero five B-T-C.

lines.text: Notional value is quantity times price. It's the full value of the trade.
lines.say: Notional value is quantity times price. It's the full value of the trade.

lines.text: Like 3 kg of onions at 40 per kg: the bill is 120. Here, 0.05 × 60,000 = 3,000 USDT.
lines.say: Like three kg of onions at forty per kg: the bill is one hundred twenty. Here, zero point zero five times sixty thousand equals three thousand U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Bigger size means every price move counts for more, up or down.
lines.say: Bigger size means every price move counts for more, up or down.

lines.text: Now the profit or loss formula for spot: exit minus entry, times quantity.
lines.say: Now the profit or loss formula for spot: exit minus entry, times quantity.

lines.text: Buy 0.05 BTC at 60,000 and sell at 61,200: 1,200 × 0.05 = +60 USDT. That's the gross result.
lines.say: Buy zero point zero five B-T-C at sixty thousand and sell at sixty-one thousand two hundred: one thousand two hundred times zero point zero five equals plus sixty U-S-D-T. That's the gross result.

lines.text: Gross means before any fees. Sell at 59,400 instead, and it's −600 × 0.05 = −30 USDT.
lines.say: Gross means before any fees. Sell at fifty-nine thousand four hundred instead, and it's minus six hundred times zero point zero five equals minus thirty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: While a trade is open, its profit or loss is unrealized. It changes with every tick.
lines.say: While a trade is open, its profit or loss is unrealized. It changes with every tick.

lines.text: A green number now can turn red a minute later. It isn't locked in until you close.
lines.say: A green number now can turn red a minute later. It isn't locked in until you close.

lines.text: When you exit, it becomes realized: the result is fixed. Here, +60 USDT, before fees.
lines.say: When you exit, it becomes realized: the result is fixed. Here, plus sixty U-S-D-T, before fees.

lines.text: Futures next. On a USDT-margined contract, a long works the same way: exit minus entry, times size.
lines.say: Futures next. On a U-S-D-T-margined contract, a long works the same way: exit minus entry, times size.

lines.text: Long 0.1 BTC at 60,000, exit at 59,400: −600 × 0.1 = −60 USDT. A loss.
lines.say: Long zero point one B-T-C at sixty thousand, exit at fifty-nine thousand four hundred: minus six hundred times zero point one equals minus sixty U-S-D-T. A loss.

lines.text: This is simplified: fees and funding are left out for now.
lines.say: This is simplified: fees and funding are left out for now.

lines.text: Leverage doesn't change this USDT result, but it makes it larger compared with your margin.
lines.say: Leverage doesn't change this U-S-D-T result, but it makes it larger compared with your margin.

lines.text: For a short, flip it: entry minus exit, times size.
lines.say: For a short, flip it: entry minus exit, times size.

lines.text: Short 0.1 BTC at 60,000, exit at 59,400: 600 × 0.1 = +60 USDT. The fall was your gain.
lines.say: Short zero point one B-T-C at sixty thousand, exit at fifty-nine thousand four hundred: six hundred times zero point one equals plus sixty U-S-D-T. The fall was your gain.

lines.text: But exit at 60,800, and it's −800 × 0.1 = −80 USDT. A short loses when the price rises.
lines.say: But exit at sixty thousand eight hundred, and it's minus eight hundred times zero point one equals minus eighty U-S-D-T. A short loses when the price rises.

lines.text: Now fees. Say you go long 0.1 BTC from 60,000 to 60,600. Gross: +60 USDT.
lines.say: Now fees. Say you go long zero point one B-T-C from sixty thousand to sixty thousand six hundred. Gross: plus sixty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Exchanges charge a fee on entry and again on exit: notional value times the fee rate.
lines.say: Exchanges charge a fee on entry and again on exit: notional value times the fee rate.

lines.text: We'll use 0.05%, a made-up rate. Entry fee: 6,000 × 0.05% = 3.00 USDT.
lines.say: We'll use zero point zero five percent, a made-up rate. Entry fee: six thousand times zero point zero five percent equals three U-S-D-T.

Exit fee: six thousand sixty times zero point zero five percent equals three point zero three U-S-D-T. Net: sixty minus three minus three point zero three equals plus fifty-three point nine seven U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Net is what you actually keep. Always check real fee rates before trading.
lines.say: Net is what you actually keep. Always check real fee rates before trading.

lines.text: A common mistake: counting the gross result and forgetting fees.
lines.say: A common mistake: counting the gross result and forgetting fees.

lines.text: Long 0.1 BTC from 60,000 to 60,040. Gross: +4 USDT. Looks like a win.
lines.say: Long zero point one B-T-C from sixty thousand to sixty thousand forty. Gross: plus four U-S-D-T. Looks like a win.

lines.text: But fees are 3.00 on entry and about 3.00 on exit. Net: about −2 USDT. A gross win, a net loss.
lines.say: But fees are three on entry and about three on exit. Net: about minus two U-S-D-T. A gross win, a net loss.

lines.text: And remember: an open, unrealized profit isn't yours until you close.
lines.say: And remember: an open, unrealized profit isn't yours until you close.

lines.text: Your turn. Short 0.02 BTC at 60,000, closed at 61,000. What's the gross result? Pause if needed.
lines.say: Your turn. Short zero point zero two B-T-C at sixty thousand, closed at sixty-one thousand. What's the gross result? Pause if needed.

lines.text: Gross: −20 USDT. Entry minus exit is −1,000, times 0.02.
lines.say: Gross: minus twenty U-S-D-T. Entry minus exit is minus one thousand, times zero point zero two.

lines.text: With 0.05% fees, 0.60 on entry and 0.61 on exit, the net is −21.21 USDT.
lines.say: With zero point zero five percent fees, zero point six on entry and zero point six one on exit, the net is minus twenty-one point two one U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Before you go on, the risks.
lines.say: Before you go on, the risks.

lines.text: Prices can jump past the exit you planned, so your real exit can be worse.
lines.say: Prices can jump past the exit you planned, so your real exit can be worse.

lines.text: Fees hit every entry and exit, and futures add funding. Small trades feel it most.
lines.say: Fees hit every entry and exit, and futures add funding. Small trades feel it most.

lines.text: Leverage makes the same loss a bigger share of your margin, and can lead to liquidation.
lines.say: Leverage makes the same loss a bigger share of your margin, and can lead to liquidation.

lines.text: These are simple models, not predictions. Choosing no trade is always allowed.
lines.say: These are simple models, not predictions. Choosing no trade is always allowed.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Long or spot: exit minus entry, times quantity. Short: entry minus exit.
lines.say: Long or spot: exit minus entry, times quantity. Short: entry minus exit.

lines.text: Unrealized results move with the price. Realized results are fixed when you close.
lines.say: Unrealized results move with the price. Realized results are fixed when you close.

lines.text: Net is gross minus fees, and on futures, funding too.
lines.say: Net is gross minus fees, and on futures, funding too.

lines.text: Check yourself: long 0.1 BTC from 60,000 to 60,300, with 6 USDT in total fees. What's the net?
lines.say: Check yourself: long zero point one B-T-C from sixty thousand to sixty thousand three hundred, with six U-S-D-T in total fees. What's the net?

lines.text: Gross is 300 × 0.1 = 30 USDT. Minus 6 in fees: net +24 USDT.
lines.say: Gross is three hundred times zero point one equals thirty U-S-D-T. Minus six in fees: net plus twenty-four U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Next up, T07: market, limit and stop orders. See you there!
lines.say: Next up, T seven: market, limit and stop orders. See you there!
